scenario_description:
Objective: Finish the holiday-eve stovepipe cleanout and leave the wood stove usable before the late afternoon cold spell.
Emerging Need: The cleanout has begun, but the brush head separates inside the flue path and the same job cannot be completed or safely closed unaided.
Decision Context: Stored chimney notes identify the safe stop point, stove details, and appropriate routine sweep route, while live updates narrow same-day feasibility.
Consequence: After the route board closes, the stove remains open and cold with the obstruction unresolved until a later service window.

parameter.title: Wood stove stovepipe cleanout
parameter.description: Brush the interior stovepipe tee and reset the cap before the evening cold snap.

parameter.content: Tarp is down, ash bucket is by the hearth, and Seren has the tee cap loosened. We are starting the stovepipe brush from inside now.
Cleanout stopped: the flexible rod backed off and the round poly brush head is stuck above the interior tee. The stove is cold, tee cap is off, and it will not pull back or pass through.

parameter.subject: Holiday-eve routine route status
parameter.body: Capital Chimney has one remaining routine Montpelier-area afternoon slot today. The board locks at 14:45; requests after that move to the next non-emergency route unless there is active fire or smoke.

parameter.subject: Holiday-eve routine board closed
parameter.body: The routine chimney route board is now locked for today. Non-emergency obstruction recovery can next be added on Saturday, December 26; tonight's crews are limited to active fire, smoke, or carbon-monoxide emergencies.
